format: html
execute:

On this page, you can find many simulated datasets to use for the final project. Your are free to simulate your own data, but these are provided for convenience. 

```{r}
library(stringr)
all.files <- list.files('data/', pattern = '.csv') %>% 
  str_sort(numeric = T)
one.mean <- all.files[str_detect(all.files, 'one-mean')]
one.prop <- all.files[str_detect(all.files, 'one-prop')]
two.mean <- all.files[str_detect(all.files, 'two-mean')]
two.prop <- all.files[str_detect(all.files, 'two-prop')]
paired <- all.files[str_detect(all.files, 'pair')]
```


## Proportions

In these datasets, 0 represents a "failure" and 1 represents a "success". Taking the average of the response columns (per group) will provide the sample proportion of success.

::: {layout-ncol=2}

### One Proportion

```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(paste0(
  "- [", one.prop, "]",
  "(data/", one.prop, ")\n"
))
```

### Two Proportions

```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(paste0(
  "- [", two.prop, "]",
  "(data/", two.prop, ")\n"
))
```

:::

## Means

These are the numeric responses for each observation. For the paired data, you will need to calculate the difference between the "first" and "second" columns.

::: {layout-ncol=3}

### One Mean

```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(paste0(
  "- [", one.mean, "]",
  "(data/", one.mean, ")\n"
))
```

### Two Means

```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(paste0(
  "- [", two.mean, "]",
  "(data/", two.mean, ")\n"
))
```

### Paired Data

```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(paste0(
  "- [", paired, "]",
  "(data/", paired, ")\n"
))
```

:::
